lines.text: In June 2003, NASA shared this animation of the plan.
lines.speaker: nova

lines.text: That was the plan. Now let's make it happen!
lines.speaker: nova

lines.text: Pull down to start the engines.
lines.speaker: nova

lines.text: Liftoff! Push up to climb.
lines.speaker: nova

lines.text: The boosters separate. The upper stage carries Opportunity onward.

lines.text: Opportunity launched July 7, 2003, at 11:18 p.m. EDT, at night!
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Its Delta II Heavy rocket had nine strap-on boosters.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The launch glare briefly lit up Florida's beaches.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In real life, the launch team and computers controlled it. Here, you help.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The trip to Mars took about six and a half months.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The heat shield protected Opportunity as it entered the thin Martian air.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: A parachute opened to slow the fall.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The heat shield fell away.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The lander lowered on a rope beneath the backshell.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Giant airbags inflated around the lander.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Rockets on the backshell slowed the fall almost to a stop.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The rope was cut. The airbag ball dropped and bounced across the plain.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It rolled into a small crater. Scientists called it a hole-in-one!
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: January 24, 2004 (U.S. time). January 25 in UTC.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The airbags deflated and pulled back.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The lander opened its petals like a flower.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Opportunity unfolded its solar panels and camera mast.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It slowly drove onto the ground, leaving its first wheel tracks.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Opportunity woke up inside a small crater on a plain called Meridiani.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: All around were tiny round pebbles. Scientists nicknamed them 'blueberries.'
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: They're really grey. They looked blue in special false-colour pictures.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: They formed inside rocks that were soaked by water long ago.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Clues showed this place was once the shore of a salty sea.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Opportunity ran on sunlight. Dust slowly covered its solar panels.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But Martian winds sometimes blew the dust away, and its power came back.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Once, it got stuck in a sand dune for over a month.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Engineers on Earth carefully drove it out.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It kept exploring, crater after crater.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It became the first robot to drive farther than a marathon on another world.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It reached Endeavour crater, about 22 kilometres wide.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In 2018, a giant dust storm covered Mars and blocked the sunlight.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Opportunity went quiet on June 10, 2018.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Engineers sent more than a thousand messages, hoping it would wake.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It was planned for 90 Martian days. It worked about 60 times longer.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It drove 45 kilometres in all. It rests in Perseverance Valley today.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In 2026, the rover Perseverance drove even farther, continuing the journey.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Opportunity landed in 2004 with a hole-in-one.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It found blueberries: clues of water.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Wind cleaned its solar panels.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The first robot beyond a marathon on another world.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: It worked about 60 times longer than planned.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Ready for a mini-game?
lines.speaker: nova

lines.text: Be the wind. Wipe the dust from the solar panels.
lines.speaker: nova

lines.text: Pinch a grey pebble. Drop it in the Science Box.
lines.speaker: nova

lines.text: Point at a dust devil, then steer it over the panels.
lines.speaker: nova

lines.text: Clear the panels to wake it up!
lines.speaker: nova

lines.text: You made it to sol 90, the whole planned mission!
lines.speaker: nova

lines.text: The real Opportunity kept going about 60 times longer than planned!
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Grey hematite! It formed in water long ago.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Martian winds and whirlwinds really cleaned rover panels!
